segments.text: "Welcome to Daily Robotics Digest, your daily dose of the latest news from the world of robotics.
July 29th, 2026 - we've got a packed show for you today.
From advancements in ROS 2 communication, to breakthroughs in humanoid robot performance, and a game-changing robotic hand for high-value manufacturing, we've got it all lined up.
Let's dive into today's top stories!"
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: Learning Zenoh: A New Communication Layer for ROS 2."
The author has successfully explored and implemented Zenoh in practical robotics scenarios as part of a study to assess its behavior and performance compared to the default DDS-based setup.

The author's approach involved designing and testing various robotic applications utilizing both the conventional DDS (Data Distribution Service) protocol, which is currently used by ROS 2, and the lightweight Zenoh communication layer, with a focus on resource-constrained hardware systems and cross-network communication.
This was accomplished through an experimental methodology involving robot development, simulation environments, network simulations, and performance metrics analysis.
The results of this assessment reveal that Zenoh offers advantages in terms of reduced latency and bandwidth usage over DDS-based setups.

This outcome has significant implications for the AI and tech industries, particularly with regards to the growing demand for edge computing, IoT connectivity, and real-time data processing in robotics and automation applications.
As researchers continue to explore and refine the capabilities of Zenoh, it's likely that this new communication layer will play a key role in shaping the future of ROS 2-based systems.
From The Robot Report, "How integrated actuators improve humanoid robot joint performance and system integration,"
a new study reveals that integrated actuators significantly enhance the overall performance and integration of humanoid robots.
Researchers have developed compact modules combining multiple components into one unit, resulting in reduced weight, simplified wiring requirements, and improved mechanical layout.
These advancements were made possible by the development of actuator modules such as the AK45-10, which boasts a 7Nm peak torque output through a 10:1 planetary gearbox.
By integrating these actuators, humanoid robots can now achieve enhanced joint performance and system integration.
The new technology is expected to play a crucial role in future robotics advancements.
This breakthrough promises to further accelerate innovation in the AI and tech industry, enabling more sophisticated and efficient humanoid robots to be developed.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Tacta Systems unveils AI-powered robotic hand for high-value manufacturing"
, Tacta Systems has introduced a robotics platform, TactaBot, designed to bring human-like dexterity and touch to industrial automation.

The platform combines a robotic hand, a wearable skill capture system, and an artificial intelligence engine that enables robots to perform complex manufacturing tasks requiring precision, adaptability, and tactile feedback.
The Tacta Hand at the centre of the platform features 15 independently actuated joints and pairs with tactile sensors to detect force and temperature.
This allows for precise assembly of components such as precision electronics and wire harnesses traditionally difficult for robots.
The integrated system enables robots to adapt to different manufacturing processes and make adjustments on the fly, increasing efficiency and reducing errors.
The introduction of TactaBot marks a significant advancement in industrial automation, enabling robots to tackle high-value tasks previously thought to be exclusive to human capabilities.
This breakthrough has implications for the AI/tech industry, as it paves the way for more sophisticated robotic systems capable of mimicking human dexterity and precision.
From IEEE Spectrum - Robotics, "Robot Finger Feels in Color,"
a team of scientists has developed a robotic fingertip with synthetic skin that reflects different colors of light in response to mechanical deformation.
This innovation enables the creation of high-resolution maps of topology, strain, and contact pressure, marking a significant breakthrough in tactile sensing technology.

The development of this sensor involves embedding tactile sensing directly into the material of the finger, which translates mechanical deformation into digital signals without relying on traditional taxels or pixels.
The synthetic skin uses a Bragg reflector, deformed by an object to change the reflected wavelengths, thereby providing 100-micrometer resolution with no computational latency.
This technology promises to revolutionize robotic capabilities.
The implications of this breakthrough extend beyond robotics, as researchers now have access to a more accurate and responsive way to interact with their environment.
The development of this sensor paves the way for further advancements in AI-driven technologies, where tactile feedback is increasingly becoming essential for machine learning and sensory perception.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Neura Robotics expands global physical AI training network in partnership with RWTH Aachen University."
Neura Robotics has partnered with RWTH Aachen University to establish a new Neura Gym in Germany, scheduled to open by the end of 2026.
The facility will be part of a worldwide network of Physical AI training centers where robots can be trained using real-world environments and simulation to generate data for AI development.

As part of this initiative, ten Neura Gyms are currently under development, with five expected to be operational across Europe, the US, and China by the end of 2026, addressing the shortage of real-world training data in Physical AI.
From Robotics & Automation News, "NoTip launches public beta of robotic food delivery platform in Ohio".
NoTip has successfully launched a public beta of its robotic food delivery platform in Mason, Ohio, allowing residents to participate and gather feedback on the service.
The company's innovative dual-stage delivery system uses an electric road vehicle to transport orders before a robot completes the final doorstep delivery.

This unique approach streamlines the delivery process, while customers pay a flat $6 delivery fee with no tipping or restaurant price mark-ups, providing a seamless experience for both users and restaurants.
From MIT Technology Review - AI & Emerging Tech, "The AI Hype Index: Unsexy AI".

This story highlights the advancements in various AI areas that are gaining attention despite not being flashy or highly publicized, such as a new technique that has improved language models and a promising approach to chipmaking.
A company's robotic hands, designed to demonstrate advanced dexterity, sparked debate among tech enthusiasts about what constitutes "sexy" technology.
Meanwhile, researchers have made progress in natural language processing by developing a new technique that helps improve the capabilities of language models.
This breakthrough enhances the accuracy and efficiency of language-based AI applications, such as chatbots and virtual assistants.
Additionally, a team has made significant strides in chipmaking using a promising approach that could lead to faster and more efficient computing hardware.
These developments demonstrate progress in various AI areas, including natural language processing and artificial intelligence for science.
With these advancements, researchers are further expanding the capabilities of AI systems, paving the way for future innovations and applications in fields like healthcare and education.
From The Robot Report, "Registration is open for RoboBusiness 2026".
Registration is now open for RoboBusiness 2026, taking place on October 20-21, 2026, at the Santa Clara Convention Center.

The event will feature expert insights and innovative applications in robotics and AI across various sectors, with confirmed speakers including Rodney Brooks, Ken Goldberg, Jonathan Hurst, Bhavna Chandrashekhar, Morgan Pope, and Dermott O’Driscoll, among others.
Over 100 exhibitors will showcase the latest enabling technologies, products, and services on the show floor.
Attendees can now secure their spots at this premier event for the robotics and AI industry.
From The Robot Report, "ENvue Medical develops robotic feeding tube placement system,"

ENVue Medical Inc. has created a new robotic feeding tube placement system called ENvue Drive that leverages artificial intelligence and real-time navigation to automatically place feeding tubes into patients with reduced risk of complications.

This innovation utilizes electromagnetic guidance during the enteral feeding tube placement process, providing physicians with visibility while placing the tube through a sensor located at the end of the feeding tube.
By employing robotic-assisted procedural execution, ENvue Drive minimizes the chances of misplaced tubes ending up in the lungs, which can lead to severe health issues.

The development of ENvue Drive paves the way for further advancements in medical robotics and artificial intelligence, with potential implications for the improvement of patient care and outcomes in the healthcare industry.
From Robotics & Automation News, "FCC updates covered list to include foreign-produced advanced robotic devices and power inverters."

The US Federal Communications Commission has updated its Covered List to include foreign-produced advanced robotic devices and power inverters, following determinations by a White House-convened interagency body that these products pose unacceptable risks to national security.
This update was made in response to concerns about supply chain vulnerabilities and cybersecurity risks, which could be exploited by foreign governments or malign actors.

Following this determination, producers of affected devices are eligible for Conditional Approval from the Departments of War and Homeland Security to receive FCC equipment authorizations, while existing models remain unaffected.
Producers can now seek approval for their products under the new framework.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Intelligrated, Trew and Transnorm unite to create ‘leading warehouse automation provider’".

The American Industrial Partners has completed the acquisition of Honeywell Technologies Warehouse and Workflow Solutions, resulting in a single entity offering world-class warehouse automation solutions across various industries.

The combined organization, led by CEO Alfred Rebello, operates as a cohesive unit focused on providing comprehensive portfolio of equipment, software, and services to optimize operations, modernize fulfillment networks, and prepare for future challenges.
With the acquisition, over $1 billion in revenue and more than 3,700 employees across North America, South America, Europe, and Asia are now under a single entity.
The integration aims to streamline processes and leverage expertise to deliver tailored solutions.

The merger brings together Intelligrated, Trew, and Transnorm under a unified brand, positioning the company as a leading provider in warehouse automation for retail, e-commerce, manufacturing, distribution, and parcel operations.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Sapphire launches AMD-powered robotics platform for physical AI applications".
Sapphire Technology has unveiled its EDGE+ Apex SOM/Carrier Robotics Platform, a production-ready hardware platform designed to support the development of autonomous robots.
The platform features AMD Ryzen AI Embedded X100 Series processors, delivering perception, planning and control performance with up to 128GB of LPDDR5x memory.
A purpose-built robotics carrier board provides a robust foundation for continuous industrial operation, while an open software ecosystem facilitates collaboration among developers.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Kall Morris tests orbital 'tow truck' for space debris removal aboard International Space Station."

Kall Morris Inc has successfully tested its Responsive Engaging Arms for Captive Care and Handling (REACCH) system on the International Space Station, where it underwent over 170 capture trials to refine its technology.

The ISS National Laboratory provided a unique opportunity for engineers to hone their system's capabilities, which is designed to capture, relocate, and remove space debris using a robotic system with tentacle-like arms and gecko-inspired adhesive pads.
This technology has the potential to steer satellites away from collisions, extend satellite life through servicing missions, and guide obsolete spacecraft towards controlled deorbiting.
Kall Morris' innovation is poised to have a significant impact on the AI and tech industry as it paves the way for more efficient space debris removal methods.
From The Robot Report, "Agency Tool Company wants to make OTA software updates easier"

, Agency Tool Company's new startup seeks to build fast, reliable infrastructure for robotics developers by launching ATC Deploy, a software update tool that ships software to robots wherever they are.
This system works with existing deployment strategies and architectures, allowing customers to continue using their own operating systems, docker images, and file structures.

By addressing the industry's bottleneck on software updates, which can be affected by flaky connections and limited resource availability on devices, ATC Deploy aims to improve the efficiency of OTA updates for robotics developers.
"Thanks for tuning in, robotic rebels!
Until tomorrow, when we'll gear up with the latest updates and discoveries from the world of robotics - may your circuits be lit and your algorithms be zen.
See you then!"
